description: drowzeys' two-Spark launch of the stock deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark checkpoint (MIT, ungated, 167 GB) with DSpark speculative decoding (k=5), an experimental nvfp4_ds_mla 4-bit KV cache and a 1,500,000-token window, TP=2 over RoCE/IB. Upstream's standing profile: 12 sequences, GPU memory 0.85, 8192 batched tokens, B12X MoE and B12X WO projection, prefix caching, thinking off, temperature 0. Upstream reports (not measured here) a 3.23M-token KV pool, C1 about 51 tok/s, C12 about 255 tok/s aggregate, 61 to 67 percent DSpark acceptance and needle recall to 543,994 tokens. The runtime is drowzeys' published stage-c image (aidendle94 GB10 base plus Rafael Caricio's DSpark overlay plus tonyd2wild's nvfp4 stages); upstream's launcher names it vllm-dspark-runtime:dspark-nvfp4-stage-c and this recipe pins ghcr.io/drowzeys/vllm-dspark-nvfp4-stage-c:gb10 (2026-07-01), which drowzeys' companion repo documents as that image. Upstream's ghcr.io/drowzeys/dspark-nvfp4-stage-c is not publicly pullable. Licences: repo Apache-2.0, checkpoint MIT. Not gated. GB10 fit: the 0.761055 GPU utilization is vLLM's startup budget beside the absolute KV pool. Absolute KV correction: 15,998,753,178 bytes per rank, the pool of the hardware-passed DeepSeek V4 Flash DSpark vLLM duals (same weights per rank). Concurrency 6 is the most 278,528-token requests that pool holds under the pinned cache-geometry allocation bound; it bounds the scheduler, while vLLM's own accounting on this image fits about 3 full 278,528-token requests in this pool. Context stays capped from the creator profile's 1,500,000 tokens to 278,528: vLLM's accounting on this image needs about 23 GB of KV cache for one 1,500,000-token request. The declared per-rank peak (109,382,703,023 bytes) is the 79.52 GiB of weights vLLM loads per rank, this pool and 8 GB runtime overhead. Physical acceptance remains pending.
title: DeepSeek V4 Flash DSpark NVFP4-KV 1.5M vLLM two Sparks (drowzeys)
